title: 15.4 A Neuroprosthetic SoC with Sensory Feedback Featuring Frequency-Splitting-Based Wireless Power Transfer with 200Mb/s 0.67pJ/b Backscatter Data Uplink and Unsupervised Multi-Class Spike Sorting
problem: High-channel neural implants enable prosthetic control but lack closed-loop sensory feedback, limiting stability and requiring steep user learning curves. Traditional external feedback introduces latency; electrical stimulation is viable but must reject stimulation artifacts to avoid false feedback loops.
motivation: Closed-loop sensory feedback from motor cortex signals to sensory cortex modulation accelerates prosthetic learning and improves control accuracy; integrated wireless power + data uplink enables fully implantable operation without percutaneous connectors.
method: The system uses different radio frequencies to simultaneously deliver power and transmit data wirelessly without interfering with each other (called frequency-splitting). The implant sends neural signals back using backscatter—reflecting external radio waves with minimal power—at 200 megabits per second using just 0.67 trillionths of a joule per bit. A processor inside the implant automatically identifies and groups neuron firing patterns (spike sorting) without needing training data, so it only transmits categorized signals instead of raw data. A circuit filters out electrical noise from stimulation pulses during simultaneous recording, preventing false feedback loops.
key_novelty: Frequency-splitting—using separate radio frequencies for wireless power and data (200 Mb/s backscatter)—enables the implant to run without a large battery by receiving power and sending neural signals simultaneously without interference.
contributions: Frequency-splitting wireless power transfer separates power and data carriers for crosstalk-free operation
Backscatter data uplink achieves 200 Mb/s at 0.67 pJ/b energy efficiency
Unsupervised multi-class spike sorting reduces neural data bandwidth on-chip
Stimulation artifact rejection enables true closed-loop sensory feedback without artifacts
baselines: Centralized spike sorting with external processing
limitations: Not discussed; implant lifetime, wireless power range, and sorting accuracy not specified.
primary_theme: Implantable prosthetic SoC with closed-loop feedback
